title: Credit card billing-error dispute - federal basics
facts: The Fair Credit Billing Act provides a process for disputing qualifying billing errors on open-end credit accounts such as credit cards.
To preserve FCBA billing-error rights, a written billing-error notice generally must reach the creditor within 60 days after the first statement containing the error was sent.
The creditor generally must acknowledge the dispute within 30 days unless it resolves the matter sooner, and must resolve it within two complete billing cycles, not exceeding 90 days.
Consumers may have additional network, issuer or other legal protections, but those should not replace the federal deadline when FCBA rights are relevant.
